name: Pinpraise for Google Reviews – Widget, Slider & Badge
author: gatemi

sections.description:
Show all your Google reviews on your website, for free.

Pinpraise for Google Reviews is a Google reviews widget for WordPress. It puts the reviews from your Google Business Profile on your site as a slider (carousel), a grid, a list, a rating badge or a floating button, and keeps them current without you touching the page again. Add it with a block, a shortcode or a sidebar widget. No coding, and setup takes about five minutes.

  • All your reviews, not just five. Many review plugins can show only the five reviews Google hands out publicly. Pinpraise reads the reviews from your own Google Business Profile with your permission, so every one of them can go on your site: up to 1,000 in one widget.
  • Free. The plugin is free, and the free Pinpraise plan includes the website widgets for one business location. No card is asked for, and there is no trial that runs out.
  • Always current. New reviews show up on your site on their own.

What you need

  1. A WordPress site (version 6.3 or newer).
  2. A Google Business Profile that you own or manage. This is the listing with your reviews that people see on Google Search and Google Maps.
  3. A free Pinpraise account. The plugin has a button to create one.

How it works, in three steps

  1. Make your widget in Pinpraise. Create a free account at https://pinpraise.com, sign in with Google to connect your Business Profile, then open Website › Reviews on your website and create a widget. Press Get code, then Copy code.
  2. Paste the code in WordPress. Go to Settings › Pinpraise for Google Reviews and paste what you copied. The page checks it and shows a preview of your reviews.
  3. Put the reviews on a page. Press Create a Reviews page and you get a ready-made draft page. Or add the reviews to a page you already have, with the block, the shortcode or the sidebar widget.

The settings page in WordPress walks you through the same three steps.

Why is there a Pinpraise account?

Google does not let a website read all of a business’s reviews directly. Only a service the owner has given permission to can do that. Pinpraise is that service: you sign in with Google once, Pinpraise reads your reviews, and this plugin shows them on your site. That is why you see all your reviews here and not only five.

What you can choose

  • Five looks: sliding cards, grid, list, a small rating badge, or a floating button in the corner of the page.
  • Which reviews show: the lowest star rating to include, only reviews with text or all of them, newest first or highest first, and how many (up to 1,000). You can also hide single reviews.
  • What each review shows: your replies, dates, and the photos customers added. A header with your rating and a “Write a review” button can sit above the reviews.
  • Colours and style: light or dark, your own accent colour, corner shape, and your site’s font.
  • Language of the labels (such as “Read more”): English, Spanish, Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi or Tamil. The reviews themselves stay as your customers wrote them.

All of this is set in Pinpraise, under Website › Reviews on your website. A change there reaches your site within a few minutes; you do not edit the page again.

Built to stay out of the way

  • Light: one small script, loaded only on pages that show reviews. No jQuery, no cookies, no tracking of visitors across sites.
  • Your theme cannot break the reviews, and the reviews cannot change your theme (they render in a Shadow DOM).
  • Works with the block editor, the classic editor, Elementor, Divi and WPBakery, and with caching plugins.
  • Fits phones, tablets and desktops.

What is free and what is paid

Showing your Google reviews with this plugin is free, for one business location. The free Pinpraise plan also gives you an inbox for your Google reviews, where you can reply to them, and a review link with a QR code to hand to customers.

Paid Pinpraise plans add more: asking customers for reviews by email, text or WhatsApp, AI-drafted replies, reports, Google posts and more locations. You do not need any of them to show your reviews. Plans are listed at https://pinpraise.com.

Pinpraise is an independent service. This plugin is not made, endorsed or sponsored by Google; Google and Google Business Profile are trademarks of Google LLC.

External services

This plugin relies on Pinpraise (https://pinpraise.com), a third-party service, to show your reviews. Without a Pinpraise account the plugin shows nothing to visitors.

  • What is loaded and when: only on pages where a Pinpraise shortcode, block or sidebar widget is placed, the visitor’s browser downloads the widget script (https://pinpraise.com/assets/widget/pinpraise-widget.min.js) and then the review data for that widget’s key from the same address. If you set a white-label address in Settings › Pinpraise for Google Reviews, both come from that address instead. In wp-admin the widget script is loaded on one screen only, Settings › Pinpraise for Google Reviews, to show you a preview of your own widget once it is set up; that preview is not counted as a view.
  • What data is sent: the widget key, and the standard information any browser sends with a web request (IP address, user agent, the page address as referrer). When the widget scrolls into view, the script sends one view count for that widget, and clicks inside the widget are counted the same way, so the account owner sees how it is used. If the account owner turns on page statistics, these counts also carry the page path without its query string. If the account owner turns on the Google Analytics option and your site already has its own Google tag, the widget adds its view and click events to your page’s dataLayer; the widget loads no Google script itself. No cookies or browser storage are used and visitors are not tracked across sites.
  • Images from Google: reviewer profile photos and review photos are shown from where the review platform hosts them (for Google reviews, Google’s image servers such as googleusercontent.com), so the visitor’s browser requests those images directly. They are requested with no referrer. Google’s privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Checking your widget: when you save a widget code in Settings › Pinpraise for Google Reviews, and at most once an hour while you have that settings screen open, your WordPress server asks https://pinpraise.com/w/<key>.json (or your white-label address) whether the widget exists, so the screen can tell you it is connected and name the business. Only the key is sent. Nothing is asked while visitors browse your site.
  • Business info (optional): when you enter a business info key, your WordPress server reads your business details (name, address, phone, opening hours) from https://pinpraise.com/ls/<key>.json (or your white-label address) at most twice a day and adds them to your home page for search engines. Only the key is sent. Without a key nothing is fetched.
  • Where the reviews come from: Pinpraise reads them from your Google Business Profile with your permission. The plugin itself never contacts Google.

Pinpraise terms of service: https://pinpraise.com/terms.html
Pinpraise privacy policy: https://pinpraise.com/privacy.html
sections.installation:
No coding is needed. The whole setup takes about five minutes.

Install the plugin

  1. In WordPress, go to Plugins › Add New and search for “Pinpraise”.
  2. Press Install Now on Pinpraise for Google Reviews, then Activate.

Set it up

  1. Go to Settings › Pinpraise for Google Reviews.
  2. Step 1 on that page: press Create a free account. In Pinpraise, sign in with Google to connect your Business Profile, open Website › Reviews on your website, create a widget, press Get code and then Copy code.
  3. Step 2: come back to WordPress, paste what you copied and press Save and check. You should see “Connected” with your business name, and a preview of your reviews.
  4. Step 3: press Create a Reviews page. WordPress makes a draft page with your reviews on it. Open it, look it over and press Publish.

Other places to put the reviews

  • On a page you already have: edit the page, press the + button, search for “Pinpraise” and choose the Pinpraise for Google Reviews block.
  • With a page builder (Elementor, Divi, WPBakery) or the classic editor: paste the shortcode [pinpraise_reviews] where the reviews should go.
  • In a sidebar or footer: Appearance › Widgets, then add Pinpraise for Google Reviews.

To install from a ZIP file instead, use Plugins › Add New › Upload Plugin, then follow the same steps from step 3.
sections.faq:
Is it really free to show all my Google reviews?

Yes. The plugin is free, and the website widgets are part of the free Pinpraise plan for one business location. No card is asked for and the free plan has no end date. Paid plans add other things, such as asking customers for reviews and more locations; you do not need them to show your reviews.

What do I need before I start?

A WordPress site, a Google Business Profile that you own or manage, and a free Pinpraise account. You need to be able to sign in to the Google account that manages the Business Profile.

Do I need a Pinpraise account? Why?

Yes, and a free one is enough. Google lets only a service the business owner has approved read all of a business’s reviews. Pinpraise is that service: it reads your reviews from your Google Business Profile with your permission, and the plugin shows them. The plugin itself never talks to Google. Step 1 on the plugin’s settings page has a button to create the account.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You copy one piece of code from Pinpraise, paste it into the plugin’s settings page, and press a button to create a Reviews page.

What does Pinpraise do with access to my Google Business Profile?

When you sign in with Google, Google asks you to let Pinpraise manage your Business Profile. That is the one permission Google offers for reading reviews. Pinpraise uses it to read your reviews and business details, and to post a reply to a review only when you write one in Pinpraise. You can take the access away at any time in your Google account, under Security › Your connections to third-party apps and services.

I do not have a Google Business Profile. Can I use this?

Not yet. The reviews come from your Google Business Profile, so you need one first. Creating a profile is free at https://business.google.com. Once Google has verified it and you have reviews, come back and set up the plugin.

How many reviews can I show?

Up to 1,000 in one widget.

I see only some of my reviews. How do I show them all?

A new widget starts with a careful choice: reviews of 4 and 5 stars, only those with written text, and the newest 12. To show everything, open the widget in Pinpraise › Website › Reviews on your website and change three things: set Show ratings of to All ratings, switch off Only reviews with text, and raise Number of reviews. Save, and your site follows within a few minutes.

Can I choose which reviews show? Can I leave out bad ones?

Yes. You set the lowest star rating to include, and you can hide any single review from your website. This changes only what your website shows. The reviews on Google stay exactly as they are.

How do new reviews get onto my site?

On their own. Pinpraise checks Google for new reviews and your site shows them without you doing anything.

Where do I change the layout or colours?

In Pinpraise › Website › Reviews on your website. The plugin shows whatever the widget is set to, so nothing is configured twice. A change reaches your site within a few minutes, and you do not need to clear your caching plugin.

Can I show the reviews in my own language?

The labels around the reviews (such as “Read more” and “Based on 30 reviews”) can be in English, Spanish, Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi or Tamil. The reviews themselves are shown as your customers wrote them.

Does it show my replies and customer photos?

Yes, both, and you can switch either off in the widget’s settings.

Will the stars show next to my site in Google search results?

No, and no plugin can promise that. Google does not show star ratings in search results for reviews a business publishes about itself. The plugin shows your reviews to the people who visit your site.

Is there a “Powered by Pinpraise” line?

A small one shows under the reviews. You can switch it off in the widget’s settings.

I have more than one business location. Does it work?

Yes. The free plan covers one location. With more locations on a paid plan, you make a widget for each one (or one widget for several) and place each with its own key: [pinpraise_reviews key="…"]. The block and the sidebar widget have a field for the key too.

Can I show different reviews on different pages?

Yes. Make a second widget in Pinpraise and add its key to the shortcode on that page: [pinpraise_reviews key="…"].

Can I show reviews from Facebook, Trustpilot or Tripadvisor too?

Not at the moment. The widget shows your Google reviews.

Does it slow my site down?

No. One small script is loaded in the background, only on pages that show reviews, and the reviews are served from Pinpraise’s cache. The rest of your page does not wait for it.

Does it work with page builders and caching plugins?

Yes. The shortcode works in Elementor, WPBakery, Divi and the classic editor; the output is plain HTML that caching plugins can store.

Does it work on phones?

Yes. The reviews take the width of the place they are in and fit phones, tablets and desktops.

My reviews are not showing. What should I check?

  1. Open Settings › Pinpraise for Google Reviews. It should say “Connected” with your business name. If it says your reviews are not showing, the widget was paused or deleted in Pinpraise: open Pinpraise, switch the widget to Live, or paste the code of another widget.
  2. Check that the page is published and has the block, the shortcode or the sidebar widget on it.
  3. If the page shows a grey note that starts with “Pinpraise for Google Reviews:”, the setup is not finished. Only you see that note, visitors do not. Follow the link in it.
  4. If the widget shows “No reviews to show yet”, your widget’s choices leave no review to show. In Pinpraise, set Show ratings of to All ratings, or switch off Only reviews with text.

Still stuck? Ask on the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org and we will help.

What happens if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

The reviews stop showing on your site. Deleting the plugin also removes its settings from WordPress. Nothing changes on Google, and your Pinpraise account and widget stay as they are, so you can install the plugin again later and paste the same code. To close the Pinpraise account too, do that in Pinpraise.

What does the paid Pinpraise plan add?

Tools to get more reviews and save time: asking customers for a review by email, text or WhatsApp, AI-drafted replies, reports, Google posts and more locations. They are optional. Showing your reviews on your site stays free.

What is the “Business info key” under More options?

An optional extra on paid Pinpraise plans. It tells search engines your business name, address, phone and opening hours, kept in step with Google. Most sites can leave it empty; your reviews show without it.

What about privacy and GDPR?

The plugin stores only your widget key, the Pinpraise address and the optional business info key in the WordPress options table, plus a short-lived note of whether the widget is connected and a short-lived copy of your business details when you use the business info key. When a visitor opens a page with the widget, their browser fetches the review JSON and the widget script from Pinpraise (or the white-label address you set). The widget sets no cookies and does not track visitors across sites; it counts views and clicks per widget for the owner’s statistics, and reviewer photos load from the review platform’s image servers (Google’s for Google reviews). Details are under External services below; Pinpraise’s privacy policy is at https://pinpraise.com/privacy.html.

Where do I get help?

Ask on the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org, or write to us through https://pinpraise.com/contact.html.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • The plugin’s name now says what it does: Widget, Slider & Badge.
  • Once your reviews are connected, the settings page has a small line asking for a review of the plugin on WordPress.org. Press Hide and it stays hidden.
  • The Create a free account button tells Pinpraise the visit came from this plugin (a tag on the link, nothing about you or your site).

1.1.0

  • Settings page rebuilt as three plain steps, with a button to create a free Pinpraise account.
  • Paste the whole code from Pinpraise, the link or just the key: the plugin finds the key itself.
  • The key is checked with Pinpraise when you save, and the page shows whose reviews are connected and a live preview.
  • New: Create a Reviews page makes a draft page with your reviews on it.
  • Copy button for the shortcode; the white-label address and business info key moved under More options.
  • The block and the sidebar widget say what is left to do when setup is not finished, with a link to Settings.

1.0.0

  • First release: shortcode, block, sidebar widget, settings page, white-label address, optional business info (LocalBusiness details) on the home page.
